result.title: VibeVideoBench:Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Code-Driven Video Generation
result.summary: Diffusion video models produce striking clips, but they cannot reliably render an exact formula, a correct chart, a ruleconsistent game or narration synchronized to on-screen events. A different route is emerging: multimodal agents that write code to render every frame and synthesize every sound. We introduce VibeVideoBench, a benchmark for evaluating agents on code-driven video generation. Its 239 self-contained tasks in English and Chinese span 12 categories, from data stories and music-driven pieces to classroom lessons and paper explainers; each asks an agent, running in its native harness inside a sandbox, to deliver a finished MP4 with sound within one hour. Evaluation is hierarchical and evidence-based: program checks of the delivery spec, about 13k task-specific rubric checks traced to the requirements they enforce, and five quality dimensions anchored per task, judged by three VLM judge panels and validated with blind human preferences. Across nine frontier agent systems and 2,151 scored rollouts, the benchmark is far from solved: GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 lead clearly, yet even the best system fails a core requirement on about a quarter of tasks. Whether a video arrives at all matters as much as its quality, and three quarters of the lost videos are final renders started too late, run too slowly or never started. The judges agree with each other and with human preferences on system rankings, but only moderately on individual videos.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 VibeVideoBench：239 个中英双语任务，要求多模态 agent 在沙箱内写代码渲染画面与合成声音并在一小时内交付 MP4；评估采用程序化交付检查、约 1.3 万条任务专属 rubric 与 VLM 评审团加人工盲评的分层方式，九个前沿系统仍远未解决。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 内部视觉表示和 latent 状态生成关系较弱，但「最终渲染启动过晚或过慢导致交付失败」可供核查 agent 计算预算与停止/启动时机决策，VLM 评审团与人类仅在单视频上中等一致也可为多模态评价可靠性提供线索。
